title: Rebuild OmniStream and fix mainnet access + Watch-page Viewer Timer visibility

requirements.text: Fix the Watch page so the Viewer Timer UI is clearly visible and usable for all users on common screen sizes (mobile + desktop), including when the Watch page is reached via deep links.

quotes: Re code i can't see the timer thing

acceptanceCriteria: Opening any existing media in the Watch page displays the Viewer Timer card without requiring scrolling on desktop layouts (unless the viewport is extremely small).
On mobile, the Viewer Timer is discoverable and not hidden behind other UI elements (e.g., it appears below the player/metadata or via a clearly labeled control).
The Viewer Timer can be started and stopped, and it counts down as expected.
When the timer reaches zero, the video pauses (existing behavior preserved).

requirements.text: Fix and harden the deployed-site access path so users do not encounter the gateway error “Canister ID Not Resolved” when opening the correct icp0.io URL for the deployed OmniStream frontend assets canister.

quotes: It says Canister ID Not Resolved

acceptanceCriteria: A fresh mainnet deployment produces a working, publicly accessible HTTPS URL in the form https://<canister-id>.icp0.io that loads the OmniStream app.
The app loads successfully at the root URL (/) and does not require manual URL modifications to render the UI.
Deep links using the app’s hash routing (e.g., https://<canister-id>.icp0.io/#/watch/<title>) open the correct page directly without blank screens.

requirements.text: Update the repo-local mainnet deployment documentation to explicitly explain which deployed canister URL must be used for the public website, how to obtain it after deployment, and what a correct URL looks like (including hash-routing examples). Use English for all user-facing text.

quotes: Please paste the URL that appeared in the deploy message.
It says Canister ID Not Resolved

acceptanceCriteria: The deployment guide clearly instructs how to find the correct frontend assets canister URL after `dfx deploy --network ic`.
The guide includes at least one correct example URL format for the app root and one for a deep link using hash routing (e.g., `/#/watch/...`).
The guide includes a short troubleshooting note for the specific error text “Canister ID Not Resolved” with concrete checks (e.g., malformed URL, missing canister ID, wrong domain).

requirements.text: Add a user-facing error state in the frontend for when the app cannot reach the backend canister (or cannot create/use the actor), so the UI shows a clear English message describing that the service is temporarily unavailable instead of failing silently.

quotes: It says Canister ID Not Resolved

acceptanceCriteria: If the frontend cannot create/use the backend actor or a key query fails due to network/canister connectivity, the UI displays a clear error message in English (not just a console error).
The error state provides a minimal actionable hint (e.g., reload, verify the URL is the deployed icp0.io link) without exposing internal stack traces.
Normal behavior is unchanged when the backend is reachable.

constraints: Backend must remain a single Motoko actor in backend/main.mo; do not introduce additional backend services.
Do not edit files under frontend/src/components/ui or any other frontend immutablePaths; compose them instead.
Use English for any user-facing text.
Keep hash-based routing compatibility for Internet Computer assets canister hosting (do not switch to server-dependent routing).
nonGoals: Implementing custom domain setup (DNS) changes for ommistream.com / www.ommistream.com without the exact deployed canister URL provided by the user.
Adding new product features beyond fixing visibility/accessibility issues and deployment accessibility.
Integrating third-party analytics, SEO tooling, or external hosting/CDNs.
